claim: For \(q\ge2\), let \(W_q(y\mid x)=1/(q-1)\) when \(y\ne x\) and zero otherwise on \([q]\). In the common-randomness-assisted, fixed-codebook, worst-case total-variation model, the exact minimum codebook size for two independent uses is \(M_0^\star(W_q^{\otimes2})=4\) for \(q=2\) and \(M_0^\star(W_q^{\otimes2})=3\) for every \(q\ge3\).

correctness.rationale: The lower bound is an exact support-covering argument. For \(q\ge3\), any two neighborhoods cover at most \(q^2-2\) inputs, while three diagonal codewords with independent random coordinate injections cover every input. The stabilizer of each input acts transitively on its target support, so uniform tie-breaking yields the exact target law. For \(q=2\) the target supports are four distinct singletons, forcing four outputs.
